title: A method for reconstituting the motility of membrane-bound myosin on the surface of the cell-sized W/O droplet
author: Sato, Sumiyoshi, et al.
materials: Chemicals and Reagents:•1 M Sucrose (#30404–45, Nacalai Tesque, Japan)•1 M Glucose (#049–31165, Fujifilm Wako Pure Chemical, Japan)•100 mM ATP (#A7699, Sigma-Aldrich, USA)•132 µM Alexa488-phalloidin (#A12379, Thermo-Fisher, USA)•ATP regeneration system (500 mM creatine phosphate (#10621714001, Roche, Switzerland) and 30 mg mL⁻1 creatine phosphokinase (#10127566001, Roche, Switzerland))•Oxygen scavenging system (5 kU mL⁻1 glucose oxidase (#G2133, Sigma-Aldrich, USA) and 4 mg mL-1 catalase (#C3155, Sigma-Aldrich, USA))

steps.title: Assemble glass flow chamber
steps.instruction: Place strips of double‑sided tape (#W‑12, Scotch 3 M, USA) at 1‑mm intervals on a 24 × 36 mm silane‑coated glass coverslip. Lay a non‑treated 18 × 18 mm glass coverslip (#C218181, Matsunami Glass Industry, Japan) on top, lightly press the contact areas to form a chamber of ~3 µL volume, then after later infusion of the W/O droplet emulsion seal both ends of the flow path with vacuum grease (#60700, M&I Materials, UK). Verify that no gaps exist between coverslips, tape, and grease; the chamber is single‑use and must be checked for absence of fluid flow and droplet stability.

substeps.instruction: Place double‑sided tape strips at 1‑mm intervals on silane‑coated coverslip.
Add non‑treated coverslip on top and press lightly.
Confirm chamber volume (~3 µL) and absence of gaps.
After emulsion infusion, seal both ends with vacuum grease.

steps.title: Thaw protein stocks on ice
steps.instruction: Retrieve myosin ID (2.7 µM stock, stored at –80 °C), calmodulin (123 µM stock, stored at –80 °C), and G‑actin (60 µM stock, stored in liquid nitrogen); thaw each quickly by hand and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare 20 µL aqueous phase
steps.instruction: In a chilled tube, mix AT buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.4, 25 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM EGTA) to a final volume of 20 µL and add: 360 mM sucrose (from 1 M stock #30404‑45, Nacalai Tesque), 100 mM glucose (from 1 M stock #049‑31165, Fujifilm Wako), 1 mM ATP (from 100 mM stock #A7699, Sigma‑Aldrich), 0.7 µM myosin ID, 1.5 µM calmodulin, 1.2 µM G‑actin, 2.6 µM Alexa488‑phalloidin (from 132 µM stock #A12379, Thermo‑Fisher), ATP regeneration system (5 mM creatine phosphate from 500 mM stock #10621714001, Roche, and 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ creatine phosphokinase from 30 mg mL⁻¹ stock #10127566001, Roche), and oxygen‑scavenging system (50 U mL⁻¹ glucose oxidase from 5 kU mL⁻¹ stock #G2133, Sigma‑Aldrich, and 40 µg mL⁻¹ catalase from 4 mg mL⁻¹ stock #C3155, Sigma‑Aldrich). Keep the mixture on ice; it remains stable for several hours and can be used for multiple droplet preparations, though the aqueous phase should be prepared immediately before each experiment because overall stability is limited to a few tens of minutes.

steps.title: Infuse emulsion and seal chamber
steps.instruction: Introduce the W/O droplet emulsion containing the prepared aqueous phase into the assembled glass flow chamber, then immediately seal both ends of the flow path with vacuum grease, confirming that no fluid flow occurs and that droplets remain stable throughout the assay.

steps.title: Track actin filament movement
steps.instruction: Using Mark 2.6 software with a two‑dimensional Gaussian fitting algorithm, manually trace the x‑ and y‑coordinates of the leading edge of each gliding actin filament for every video frame, export the coordinate data, and calculate filament velocities by linear fitting of five consecutive data points from the time‑distance (xy) plots.
